title: One missing input permits four pool-rank reversals with 561 residual pairs fixed at zero in a leech model
abstract: We tested whether observing all but one input can fix the coherence rank of contact-count and equal-input pools. We used public anatomy and reference activity summaries from one leech ganglion. In a 35-input, unit-power model, we fixed the observed residual block to the identity and left one input row unknown. An exact Schur-complement bound shows that six possible omissions permit a rank reversal in at least one trial; the other 29 preserve all five ranks. One fixed missing row reverses four trial ranks while the other 561 residual pairs stay zero. Its minimum matrix eigenvalue is 0.056896. Four is the exact maximum because no single row can reverse the fifth trial. The infimum row norm for four strict reversals is 0.886208. All-mapped, confidence and square-root-magnitude samples change the number of affected omissions to 42 of 45, 4 of 21 and 5 of 35. An independent audit checked 13 source hashes, 700 spectral witness uses and 300 complex or singular bound cases. This is a conditional recording model, not a measurement of residual correlations or evidence for either pool in the animal. One animal, exact summaries, imposed unit powers and the hypothetical identity block limit inference. Code, proof, aggregate results, a figure and external regeneration steps are included.

display.caption: Conditional recording test with the observed residual block fixed to the identity. One fixed missing row reverses four trial ranks. Aggregate omission counts and sensitivity samples show where the rank remains uncertain. These are model compatibility results, not measured residual correlations.
